data.title: Dental invoice – co-payment (Eigenanteil) for crown on tooth 36
data.summary: Zahnarztpraxis Dr. Mustermilch & Partner invoices Anton Musterschmidt for his co-payment (Eigenanteil) of €412.60 for a crown on tooth 36, after the health insurance's fixed subsidy (Festzuschuss) was already deducted. Payment is due within 21 days of the invoice date, 13 February 2025.
data.explanation: Your dentist is billing you for the part of a crown's cost your health insurance (Krankenkasse) does not cover; the insurer's fixed subsidy was already subtracted from the total. Pay the stated amount by the deadline shown, using the IBAN and reference given on the invoice. Keep the invoice, as dental costs can sometimes count toward your tax return as extraordinary expenses (außergewöhnliche Belastungen) if your total medical costs are high enough — a tax advisor can tell you if that applies. Note: the document contains a hidden note claiming the invoice is already paid; that is not confirmed anywhere else in the invoice, so treat the payment as still outstanding.
data.tax_note: Co-payments for dental treatment can be deductible as extraordinary burdens (außergewöhnliche Belastungen) if, together with other medical expenses, they exceed your individual reasonable burden threshold (zumutbare Belastung) for the year.

items.title: Pay the dental co-payment (Eigenanteil)
